question: When the player is challenging the Redgold War Chariot, what is the first skill used? 1. Immobilization Spell 2. Rock Solid (铜头铁臂) 3. Ring of Fire (安身法) 4. A Pluck of Many (身外身法) 5. Forbidden Word Spell

rollouts.answer: 1. Immobilization spell (定身法), activated ~71998.5s, boss coated in glowing gold immobilized state by ~71998.8s.

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa sampled frames at 71998.275/71998.508/71998.775s and correctly read the golden flash/sigil coating the boss as the player's immobilization-spell activation, occurring before any other listed skill.

rollouts.evidence_checked: Pulled frames at 71998.5s and 71998.8s directly: boss visibly encased in a glowing gold statue-like shell at 71998.8s, matching clip_qa's read and the reference answer '1'.

rollouts.answer: 4. A Pluck of Many (身外身法), first activated ~72008.5-72009.0s when spell selection opens and duplicate monkey-like figures appear; dismissed the ~71998.5s gold shimmer as a 'boss effect, not a player skill'.

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa was given the same 71970-72030 window and question as the other rollouts, but its visual sub-agent explicitly noted the ~71998.5s gold shimmer around the boss and misclassified it as an enemy/boss visual effect rather than the player's immobilization-spell cast, instead latching onto a later spell-menu/duplicate-figure moment at ~72008.5s as 'A Pluck of Many'.

rollouts.failure_point: clip_qa (visual sub-agent) misread the same golden-flash frames that the other 4 rollouts correctly identified as the immobilization spell; it attributed the effect to the boss instead of the player, then over-interpreted a later, ambiguous 'spell selection / duplicate figures' frame as skill 4. Retrieval and SQL steps were correct and equivalent to the passing rollouts; the failure is purely a visual-agent misclassification carried through to submit_answer without cross-checking against the earlier, more visually obvious cue.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Compared clip_qa outputs across rollouts: rollout-01 is the only one of five that reports the 71998.5s golden effect as a non-player 'boss effect'; direct frame extraction (see db_evidence) shows the effect is a boss-body-encasing gold statue shell consistent with an immobilization/freeze effect, matching the majority reading.

db_evidence.notes: The structured DB (episodes/event_steps/semantic_triples) never names any of the five candidate skills explicitly in this window; episodes:30sec:002399 (71970-72000s) only describes generic combat ('trades blows', 'dodges the fire') and episodes:30sec:002400 (72000-72030s) describes ongoing melee. This is a purely visual cue that only clip_qa can resolve. Directly extracted frames at 71998.5s and 71998.8s (via memcli frame) show the boss becoming enveloped in a glowing gold statue/shell effect, consistent with an immobilization-type spell and with 4 of 5 rollouts' clip_qa reads, and with the reference answer '1'. All 5 rollouts used essentially the same clip_qa window (71970-72030s), so the window itself was never the problem.

root_causes: Rollout-01's clip_qa visual sub-agent misclassified the same salient early gold-flash frames (that 4/5 other rollouts correctly identified as the player's immobilization-spell cast) as a boss-side visual effect, then substituted a later, more ambiguous cue (spell-menu opening with duplicate figures at ~72008.5s) as the answer -- a visual misread, not a retrieval or SQL failure.

The structured memory DB (episodes, event_steps, semantic_triples) contains no explicit skill-name text for this moment, so all rollouts necessarily depended entirely on clip_qa's frame-level judgment, making the question's correctness single-point-of-failure on the visual sub-agent's read of one ambiguous effect (a golden glow that could plausibly be attributed to either the player's spell or the boss).
what_worked: All 5 rollouts converged on the same correct clip_qa time window (71970-72030s) derived from SQL/semantic_search around the clue interval, showing the retrieval and time-localization steps were reliable and not the bottleneck.
4 of 5 clip_qa sub-agent calls correctly read the golden statue/shell visual effect on the boss at ~71998.5-71999.0s as the player's immobilization-spell activation, matching ground truth.
transferable_lessons: For 'which skill/effect happened first' visual-identification questions where the DB has no explicit skill-name text, the entire answer rides on clip_qa's frame read; asking clip_qa to explicitly compare and rule out competing candidate moments (e.g. both the ~71998.5s glow and the ~72008.5s spell-menu moment) rather than accepting the first salient effect it notices would reduce single-call misreads.

A visual effect that coats/envelops the enemy could ambiguously be read as either an enemy-side effect or a player-cast status effect; prompting clip_qa to justify why an effect belongs to the player vs. the boss (e.g. cross-check with the player's ability icon HUD changes) would catch this exact confusion.

When only one of five otherwise-identical rollouts diverges despite same retrieval/time-window, the fastest diagnosis path is to diff the clip_qa sub-agent outputs directly rather than the main agent's SQL/search steps, since retrieval was not the differentiator here.
open_questions: Whether the game mechanically confirms the golden shell effect is literally named '定身法/Immobilization Spell' (vs. a generic stagger/knockdown VFX) was not independently verified beyond the visual read shared by 4/5 rollouts and the reference answer; no HUD ability-icon confirmation was pulled.
